Guideline: Inline CSS is Python strings in hdrs
Description: FastHTML renders page CSS from Python: Style() emits an unescaped <style> tag, so the stylesheet needs no compile step
Do: Put the app's CSS in one Style() block passed to fast_app(hdrs=...)
Don't: Reach for a CSS preprocessor or bundler to produce the app's stylesheet
Code Bad: # app.scss -> app.css -> Link(...); the framework never asked for the file

Guideline: Bring your own CSS with pico=False
Description: fast_app() injects PicoCSS by default and hdrs only ADD to the defaults, so supplying a stylesheet does not remove Pico
Do: Pass pico=False (or default_hdrs=False) when the app ships its own base stylesheet
Don't: Assume passing hdrs replaces the injected base layer - it is appended after it
Code Bad: app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=(Link(rel="stylesheet", href="/static/app.css"),))  # pico.min.css still loads

Guideline: Pin the versioned base stylesheet
Description: FastHTML's own base stylesheet link is an unpinned CDN URL at @latest (picocss in pico.py), so an upstream release can change base styles with no dependency bump on your app
Do: Reference an exact version for any framework base layer the app keeps
Don't: Let a production base layer resolve to a floating latest tag
Code Bad: Link(rel="stylesheet", href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@picocss/pico@latest/css/pico.min.css")

Guideline: Scope Pico with the conditional build
Description: picocondlink loads pico.conditional.min.css, which limits Pico's element styles to a class-scoped subtree instead of the whole document
Do: Load picocondlink instead of picolink when hand-written tokens own most of the page
Don't: Keep the document-wide build and override its element rules one at a time
Code Good: from fasthtml.pico import picocondlink; app, rt = fast_app(pico=False, hdrs=(*picocondlink, css))
Code Bad: app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=(css,))  # document-wide Pico still wins on bare elements

Guideline: Declare tokens on :root once
Description: Custom properties are inherited, so one :root declaration reaches every element; scattering them across rules makes the cascade, not the token layer, decide the value
Do: Declare every token in one :root block inside the app-level Style()
Don't: Redefine the same token inside a component rule so the cascade picks the winner
Code Bad: .card { --bg-primary: #f6f7f9; background: var(--bg-primary); }  # the token now depends on where the card sits

Guideline: Keep the token block out of swapped fragments
Description: A swap replaces the target's innerHTML with the returned markup, so a partial handler that returns Style(":root {...}") inserts another copy of the token layer into the page on every swap
Do: Declare tokens once in hdrs and return only markup from fragment handlers
Don't: Re-emit the :root Style() from a handler an htmx swap inserts into the page
Code Good: def panel(ref: str): return Section(P(f"Renewal for {ref}"), id="panel")  # @rt handler
Code Bad: def panel(ref: str): return Style(":root { --bg-primary: #000; }"), Section(P(f"Renewal for {ref}"), id="panel")  # @rt handler

Guideline: Declare color-scheme per palette
Description: color-scheme tells the browser which palette to use for the parts it paints itself, including form controls and scrollbars
Do: Declare color-scheme on :root in the light block and again in the dark block
Don't: Expect UA-drawn control chrome to follow your custom properties alone
Code Good: (Style(":root { color-scheme: light; --bg-primary: #fff; }"), Style("@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { color-scheme: dark; --bg-primary: #0b0d10; } }"))
Code Bad: Style(":root { --bg-primary: #0b0d10; }")  # controls keep their light palette

Guideline: Give controls their own background and colour
Description: The used colour scheme supplies the browser's default colours for form controls, and in a default app the injected Pico build paints them from --pico-form-element-* instead, so an author palette that never reaches either leaves controls reading light-on-light in a dark theme
Do: Set background and color on input, textarea and select from the same tokens as the page, or map those tokens onto --pico-form-element-*
Don't: Rely on colour inheritance, or on the framework palette, to reach form controls
Code Good: input[type=text], input[type=email], textarea, select { background: var(--bg-primary); color: var(--text-primary); border-color: var(--border-color); }
Code Bad: body { color: var(--text-primary); }  # inputs keep the UA background and colour

Guideline: Use dark_media for the dark palette
Description: dark_media() and light_media() wrap a CSS string in the matching prefers-color-scheme media query, so the block cannot be mis-typed
Do: Build the dark token overrides with dark_media() and pass the result in hdrs
Don't: Hand-write a duplicate media query per theme block
Code Good: from fasthtml.js import dark_media; app, rt = fast_app(hdrs=(light, dark_media(":root { --bg-primary: #0b0d10; --text-primary: #f5f7fa; }")))
Code Bad: Style("@media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){ :root { --bg-primary: #0b0d10; }")  # restated per block

Guideline: Nonce inline Style and Script
Description: A nonce-based CSP rejects un-nonce'd inline content, and FT tags pass an unknown attribute straight through, so Style() and Script() can carry the request nonce
Do: Pass the per-response nonce as nonce= on every inline Style() and Script()
Don't: Ship style-src 'unsafe-inline' to make inline CSS load
Code Bad: Style(css_text)  # dropped by a style-src nonce policy

Guideline: Nonce htmx's injected indicator styles
Description: htmx writes its swap-indicator CSS as an inline style tag, so a nonce-based style-src policy needs htmx.config.inlineStyleNonce
Do: Set inlineStyleNonce to the response nonce, or includeIndicatorStyles to false and write the indicator CSS yourself
Don't: Wonder why .htmx-indicator is visible when the injected style tag was blocked
Code Bad: (nothing) - htmx's inline <style> is rejected and the indicator never fades in

Guideline: Never interpolate data into Script or Style
Description: Script() and Style() write their contents without escaping, so any value interpolated into them executes or renders verbatim
Do: Pass only developer-authored literals to Script() and Style()
Don't: f-string a request value into a Script() or Style() body
Code Bad: Script(f"init({request.query_params['q']});")

Guideline: FT tags are function calls, not markup
Description: Tags are Python functions: children go in positionally and attributes arrive as keyword arguments
Do: Build every element with an FT function so FastHTML renders and escapes it
Don't: Concatenate HTML strings and hand them to the response
Code Bad:
Div("

Renewal due 14 May

", cls="policy-card")

Guideline: Attribute names use the FT aliases
Description: Named parameters become attributes, and aliases must be used for Python reserved words: cls becomes class, _for or fr becomes for; _fix_k strips leading underscores and turns remaining ones into hyphens, so data_id is data-id and aria_busy is aria-busy
Do: Use cls, _for or fr, data_*, aria_*, and unpack a dict for names with special characters
Don't: Pass class= or for= as keyword arguments, or expect a trailing underscore to be stripped
Code Bad: Label("Email", Input(id="email"), class="label", for="email", @click="go()")

Guideline: Booleans render or omit the attribute
Description: True emits the bare attribute and False or None omits it, which is how disabled, required and open should be driven from state
Do: Drive boolean HTML attributes from a Python bool
Don't: Pass the strings "false" or "no", which both render the attribute
Code Bad: Button("Submit", type="submit", disabled="false")  # still renders disabled

Guideline: Text is escaped; Safe opts out
Description: FT rendering escapes strings by default and Safe or NotStr passes trusted markup through unescaped
Do: Wrap already-sanitised markup in Safe() at the point it enters the tree
Don't: Pass raw user HTML into a tag because it "looks like markup"
Code Bad: Div(NotStr(request.form["bio"]))

Guideline: Only a lone generator child is expanded
Description: A lone generator, map or filter child is expanded for you; a list, a range, or a generator beside any sibling is not, and renders its repr into the page
Do: Pass map(fn, items) as the only child, or star-unpack a list you already built
Don't: Pass a list or range as a single child, or put a generator next to another child
Code Bad: Ul([Li(row.title) for row in rows], cls="policy-list")  # the list renders as a repr

Guideline: Components are plain functions returning FT
Description: A component is a function that returns an FT element or tuple; there is no component class, lifecycle or hook system
Do: Write components as functions taking data and returning FT
Don't: Look for a component lifecycle, props object or reactivity runtime
Code Good: def status_badge(state: str) -> FT: return Span(state.title(), cls=f"badge badge--{state}")
Code Bad: class StatusBadge: render = lambda self, state: Span(state)  # FastHTML looks for __ft__, never render

Guideline: Pass through attrs and kwargs
Description: A wrapper component forwards *args and **kwargs so callers can still add cls, id and hx_* attributes
Do: Accept *args and **kwargs in wrapper components and forward them to the inner tag
Don't: Freeze a wrapper's signature so callers cannot retarget a swap
Code Bad: def Panel(title): return Section(H2(title), cls="panel")  # no id, no hx-*

Guideline: Dataclasses render via __ft__
Description: Any object with an __ft__ method renders, so a dataclass can be a component with state
Do: Give a dataclass an __ft__ method when it owns its own markup
Don't: Thread eight positional arguments through a component that describes a record
Code Good: def __ft__(self): return Li(self.ref)  # on a @dataclass component; FastHTML calls it
Code Bad: def quote_item(ref, status, date, total, currency, owner, due, notes): ...

Guideline: Route functions double as URLs
Description: A route function used as an attribute value becomes its URL, so the link cannot drift from the route
Do: Pass the route function itself, or route.to(param=...), into href and hx_* attributes
Don't: Hand-write the path string and hope it still matches the handler
Code Bad: A("Open", href=f"/quote_detail?ref={q.ref}")

Guideline: Mutations go over POST
Description: FastHTML routes handle GET and POST by default, so a mutation should be posted rather than sent with a verb the router does not bind
Do: Use hx_post= or Form(method="post") for anything that changes state
Don't: Write hx_delete= or hx_patch= against the default route registration
Code Bad: Button("Withdraw", hx_delete=f"/withdraw?ref={q.ref}")

Guideline: Query parameters over path parameters
Description: Idiomatic FastHTML puts a handler's arguments in the query string, which is what route.to() generates
Do: Declare handler parameters and let FastHTML bind them from the query string
Don't: Define /quote/{ref} paths for an internal htmx endpoint
Code Good: def quote_detail(ref: str): ...  # bare @rt derives /quote/{ref} from the signature
Code Bad: def quote_detail(ref: str): ...  # @rt("/quote/{ref}") hardcodes a URL the signature already states

Guideline: Return the fragment, not the page
Description: A handler returns what the swap receives: Titled() is a Title plus a Main container, so returning it into a swap region puts a second main and a stray title element inside the page
Do: Return the smallest FT fragment the swap region needs
Don't: Return Titled(...) from an htmx fragment handler
Code Good: def quotes_page(page: int): return Section(quotes_table(page), id="quotes")  # @rt handler
Code Bad: def quotes_page(page: int): return Titled("Quotes", quotes_table(page))  # a second main and a title land inside the swap region

Guideline: Label wraps the control it names
Description: Every control needs a visible, programmatic label; FastHTML's documented pattern nests the control inside Label
Do: Build the field as Label(text, control) inside a Fieldset
Don't: Rely on a placeholder or a caption image to name a field
Code Bad: Input(type="email", placeholder="Email address")

Guideline: Group related fields in a Fieldset
Description: Related controls belong in one Fieldset so their shared legend is exposed with each control, which is what the framework's own form pattern does
Do: Wrap a field group in Fieldset with a Legend for the group
Don't: Use a styled Div as a visual group with no legend
Code Good: Fieldset(Legend("Card details"), Label("Number", Input(name="pan")), Label("Expiry", Input(name="expiry")))
Code Bad: Div(H3("Card details"), Input(name="pan"), Input(name="expiry"), cls="form-section")  # visually grouped, semantically nothing

Guideline: Submit buttons declare type=submit
Description: FastHTML's documented form pattern declares the submitting control explicitly, so the form's submit action is visible in the source rather than inferred
Do: Write Button("Save", type="submit") as the form's submit control
Don't: Leave the form with no declared submit control
Code Bad: Form(Label("Name", Input(name="name")), Button("Save"))

Guideline: Repopulate a rejected form with fill_form
Description: fill_form(form, obj) copies the submitted or stored values back into matching controls so a failed round-trip is not typed twice
Do: Call fill_form on the form before returning it after a validation failure
Don't: Return a blank form and make the user re-enter everything
Code Good: return fill_form(quote_form(), submitted) if errors else RedirectResponse("/quotes", status_code=303)
Code Bad: if errors: return quote_form(), errors_view(errors)  # every field is empty

Guideline: CheckboxX carries its own hidden field
Description: CheckboxX emits a Hidden with the same name before the checkbox, so an unticked box still submits a value
Do: Use CheckboxX for a preference that must arrive in the POST body either way
Don't: Hand-roll a bare Checkbox and then wonder why unticked boxes are absent from the form data
Code Bad: Checkbox(id="marketing", value="yes")  # absent from the body when unticked

Guideline: Validate the payload in the handler signature
Description: A type-annotated dataclass parameter makes FastHTML validate the posted fields before your body runs
Do: Declare the expected shape as a dataclass and take it as the handler parameter
Don't: Trust request.form[...] strings and validate them ad hoc inside the handler
Code Good: class Profile: email: str; age: int  # a @dataclass; the handler takes profile: Profile
Code Bad: def post(req: Request): age = int(req.form["age"])  # ValueError on bad input

Guideline: Close a successful POST with a redirect
Description: RedirectResponse with 303 turns the POST into a GET so a reload does not resubmit the mutation
Do: Return RedirectResponse(url=..., status_code=303) after a mutation succeeds
Don't: Render the success page directly from the POST handler
Code Bad: return Titled("Saved", P("Your quote was saved"))  # reload re-posts

Guideline: Name the field that failed
Description: An error message must identify the field in error and sit where the person reading the form will find it
Do: Render each message next to its field and repeat the field name in the text
Don't: Return only a generic "the form has errors" banner after a server round-trip
Code Good: Fieldset(Label("Expiry", Input(name="expiry", aria_invalid="true", aria_describedby="expiry-error")), P("Expiry must be MM/YY", id="expiry-error", cls="field-error"))
Code Bad: P("There were problems with your submission.", cls="error")

Guideline: Mark the rejected control aria-invalid
Description: aria-invalid on the control tells assistive technology the value was rejected, which the styled colour alone does not
Do: Set aria_invalid="true" on a control that failed server validation and point aria_describedby at the message
Don't: Signal the failure only with red border styling
Code Bad: Input(name="expiry", cls="is-invalid")  # colour only

Guideline: Keep native field reporting under htmx
Description: htmx suppresses the browser's own invalid-field reporting by default; reportValidityOfForms restores it so a bad field is announced and focused
Do: Set htmx.config.reportValidityOfForms to true in an app-level script or config
Don't: Debug an AJAX form that silently does nothing when a field is invalid
Code Bad: (left at the default) - an invalid field blocks the request with no message

Guideline: Turn validation on for non-form elements
Description: Non-form elements do not validate before a request unless hx-validate is set on them
Do: Set hx_validate="true" on a validating element that is not inside a form
Don't: Assume a contenteditable or custom widget is validated before its hx-post fires
Code Bad: Div(hx_post=save.to(), hx_target="#out", contenteditable="true")  # never validated

Guideline: Toasts need setup and a session argument
Description: The built-in toaster requires setup_toasts(app) once and an add_toast call that receives the session, so the handler must take session
Do: Call setup_toasts(app) at startup and add_toast(session, message, typ) inside a handler that accepts session
Don't: Call add_toast without a session parameter on the handler, or rely on a JS alert() instead
Code Good: def save(session, ref: str): add_toast(session, "Quote saved", typ="success")  # with setup_toasts(app, duration=5000) at startup
Code Bad: def save(ref: str): add_toast(None, "Quote saved")  # no session in scope

Guideline: Confirm a destructive action before it fires
Description: hx_confirm asks for confirmation before the request is issued, which is the cheap guard on an irreversible POST
Do: Set hx_confirm on a destructive button, and keep the message specific about what is lost
Don't: Ship a delete control with no confirmation, or one that only says "Are you sure?"
Code Good: Button("Delete quote", hx_post=drop.to(ref=q.ref), hx_confirm="Delete quote " + q.ref + "? This cannot be undone.")
Code Bad: Button("Delete", hx_post=drop.to(ref=q.ref))

Guideline: Name the swap strategy the response needs
Description: htmx defaults to innerHTML, so a response meant to replace its own trigger nests inside it unless outerHTML is declared
Do: Declare hx_swap="outerHTML" when the response replaces the element that made the request
Don't: Rely on the default swap when the response and the trigger are the same element
Code Bad: Button("Approve", hx_post=approve.to(ref=q.ref))  # the new button lands inside this one

Guideline: Swap into a named region, not the trigger
Description: hx_target sends the response elsewhere, and a FastHTML tag passed as the value resolves to its own id selector
Do: Give the receiving region an id and point hx_target or target_id at it
Don't: Let the response overwrite the button or row that triggered it
Code Bad: Div(id="panel", hx_get=panel.to(ref=q.ref))  # swaps the panel away with its own trigger

Guideline: Out-of-band updates need an id and a swap flag
Description: A response fragment with hx_swap_oob replaces the element with the same id elsewhere in the page instead of landing in the target
Do: Match the id of the region to update and set hx_swap_oob="true" on the fragment
Don't: Expect a second region to refresh from a plain fragment response
Code Good: def save(ref: str): return Div("Saved", id="alerts", hx_swap_oob="true"), status_row(ref)  # @rt handler
Code Bad: def save(ref: str): return status_row(ref)  # the alerts region never changes

Guideline: Disable the trigger while its request runs
Description: hx-disabled-elt adds the disabled attribute for the duration of the request, which is what stops a double submit
Do: Set hx_disabled_elt="this" on a submit control, or on the form's submit button
Don't: Let a slow round-trip invite a second click that runs the mutation twice
Code Bad: Button("Submit claim", type="submit", hx_post=submit.to())  # two clicks, two claims

Guideline: Include the values the handler actually needs
Description: hx-include adds extra element values to a request, so a fragment handler does not have to re-read the whole form
Do: Name the extra fields with hx_include or hx_vals instead of re-deriving them server-side
Don't: Rebuild form state from a session cache when the values are already in the DOM
Code Bad: Button("Preview", hx_get=preview.to())  # sends nothing from the form

Guideline: Boost the shell instead of rewriting every link
Description: hx-boost turns ordinary anchors and forms inside a container into AJAX requests while leaving plain hrefs working without script
Do: Put hx_boost="true" on the container that owns the navigation and keep the href values real
Don't: Rewrite every nav link as an hx-get handler just to avoid a reload
Code Bad: Nav(A("Claims", hx_get=claims, hx_target="body", hx_swap="innerHTML"))

Guideline: Preserve a live element across a swap
Description: hx-preserve keeps an element unchanged during a replacement, matched by its id, so state inside it survives
Do: Set hx_preserve on an element whose live state must outlast the swap and keep its id stable
Don't: Assume a partially filled field survives when its ancestor region is swapped wholesale
Code Bad: Textarea(name="notes", id="notes")  # draft text is lost when the panel is re-rendered

Guideline: Drive the spinner from the request class
Description: htmx adds htmx-request to the indicator element for the duration of the request and ships the .htmx-indicator CSS that fades it in
Do: Mark the spinner with class htmx-indicator and name it with hx_indicator
Don't: Hand-write a show/hide script for each request or leave a spinner permanently visible
Code Good: (Button("Load", hx_get=rows.to(), hx_indicator="#rows-spinner", hx_target="#rows"), Span("Loading rows", cls="htmx-indicator", id="rows-spinner"))
Code Bad: Span("Loading rows", cls="spinner", id="rows-spinner")  # never toggled by the request

Guideline: Hide idle indicators from assistive tech
Description: htmx's generated indicator CSS uses visibility:hidden rather than opacity alone so an idle spinner is not announced
Do: Let htmx's own indicator CSS hide the idle state instead of overriding it with opacity alone
Don't: Override .htmx-indicator with only opacity so screen readers keep reading a hidden "Loading"
Code Good: .htmx-indicator { visibility: hidden; opacity: 0; } .htmx-request .htmx-indicator, .htmx-request.htmx-indicator { visibility: visible; opacity: 1; }
Code Bad: .htmx-indicator { opacity: 0; }  # still in the accessibility tree

Guideline: Set aria-busy while a region is stale
Description: htmx toggles its own CSS classes only; FastHTML's PicoBusy() is the documented helper that sets aria-busy on the element behind a request
Do: Add PicoBusy() to the app's hdrs, or set aria-busy yourself on the swapping region between request start and finish
Don't: Assist that a busy region is announced automatically because htmx added a class to it
Code Good: from fasthtml.pico import PicoBusy; app, rt = fast_app(pico=False, hdrs=(css, PicoBusy()))
Code Bad: Div(id="rows", hx_get=rows.to())  # nothing tells a screen reader the rows are stale

Guideline: Announce the result in a status region
Description: A swapped message is silent unless it lands in a live region, so the confirmation a sighted user sees is missed entirely
Do: Swap results into a region marked role="status" with aria-live="polite"
Don't: Rely on a colour change in a swapped fragment to communicate success or failure
Code Good: Div(id="alerts", role="status", aria_live="polite")  # an out-of-band fragment swaps the result in
Code Bad: Div(id="alerts")  # the swapped "Saved" text is never announced

Guideline: Scroll the kept focus into view on purpose
Description: htmx preserves focus on an identified input between requests but does not scroll to it unless the swap asks for it
Do: Add focus-scroll:true to hx_swap when the preserved field may have moved off screen
Don't: Leave a keyboard user focused on an input that a swap has scrolled out of view
Code Bad: Input(id="expiry", hx_get=validate.to(), hx_swap="outerHTML")  # focused, invisible

Guideline: Gate htmx's state classes behind reduced motion
Description: htmx marks new content with htmx-added and the target with htmx-settling, which is where a transition belongs - and where it must stop
Do: Put the transition inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference block so the reduced-motion branch has none
Don't: Animate htmx-added or htmx-settling unconditionally
Code Bad: .htmx-settling, .htmx-added { transition: opacity 150ms ease; }  # always animates

Guideline: Turn off htmx's eval features under a strict CSP
Description: hx-on attributes, event filters and js:-prefixed hx-vals all run through eval, which htmx.config.allowEval switches off
Do: Set htmx.config.allowEval to false and keep behaviour in handlers or in a nonce'd script
Don't: Ship inline hx-on handlers to satisfy a policy that forbids eval, then debug why nothing fires
Code Bad: Button("Approve", hx_post=approve.to(), hx_on__after_request="toast('done')")  # blocked without unsafe-eval

Guideline: Keep the flex chain unbroken to the footer
Description: Each in-flow child of a flex container becomes a flex item, so a wrapper inserted between the flex body and the content is what grows, and the footer is no longer pushed down
Do: Make the direct children of the flex body grow, or make the wrapper a flex column that grows too
Don't: Add a plain Div around main and footer and expect min-height on body to hold the footer down
Code Good: body { min-height:100dvh; display:flex; flex-direction:column; } .page { flex:1 1 auto; display:flex; flex-direction:column; } .page > main { flex:1 1 auto; }
Code Bad: body { min-height:100dvh; display:flex; flex-direction:column; }  # Div(cls="page") between body and main

Guideline: Release the automatic minimum size to stop overflow
Description: A flex item's automatic minimum size keeps it from shrinking below its content, which is why a long policy reference pushes a panel out of its column
Do: Set min-width:0 (or min-height:0 on a column) on the flex item that must be allowed to shrink
Don't: Reach for overflow:hidden on the page shell to hide the resulting horizontal scroll
Code Bad: .policy-row > .reference { flex:1 1 auto; }  # long reference text widens the row

Guideline: Cap the measure on the text column
Description: Body copy needs a bounded measure; ch units tie it to the current font instead of a fixed pixel width
Do: Cap reading columns with a max-width in ch declared as a token
Don't: Let a swapped-in panel stretch body copy across the whole viewport
Code Bad: .prose { max-width: 100%; }  # 120 characters per line on a desktop viewport

Guideline: Scale type from the root with relative units
Description: rem sizes follow the user's root font size, so a token type scale survives a browser or OS text-size change
Do: Declare the type scale in rem on top of a token layer and never set a root font size below the user's default
Don't: Hard-code px font sizes on components so they ignore the user's setting
Code Good: :root { font-size: 100%; --text-body: 1rem; --text-h3: 1.25rem; --leading-body: 1.6; } body { font-size: var(--text-body); line-height: var(--leading-body); }
Code Bad: body { font-size: 16px; } .card h3 { font-size: 20px; }

Guideline: Leave the user's text spacing intact
Description: The stylesheet must not block spacing changes a person makes through their own software
Do: Use relative line height and letter spacing so user spacing overrides still take effect
Don't: Fix line-height or letter-spacing in px, or set text to a fixed height box
Code Bad: p { line-height: 24px; } .card { height: 96px; overflow: hidden; }

Guideline: Never cap pinch zoom in the viewport tag
Description: A maximum-scale or user-scalable setting stops a person magnifying the page; FastHTML's default viewport tag does not set one
Do: Keep the framework's viewport meta or write content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"
Don't: Add maximum-scale=1 or user-scalable=no to a custom Meta(name="viewport")
Code Bad: Meta(name="viewport", content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no")

Guideline: Put a skip link ahead of the repeated navigation
Description: Content that repeats on every page needs a mechanism to bypass it, and the link must come first in the tab order
Do: Emit a skip link as the first focusable element pointing at the main region's id
Don't: Make a keyboard user tab through the whole nav to reach the console
Code Good: (A("Skip to main content", href="#main", cls="skip-link"), Main("Claims table", id="main", cls="dashboard"))
Code Bad: Nav(...)  # first in the DOM, and every page repeats it

Guideline: Give the focus indicator enough contrast
Description: A focus indicator needs contrast against the colours on either side of it or keyboard users cannot see where they are
Do: Declare a focus-ring token that holds up on both surfaces and set outline-offset so it is not clipped
Don't: Ship outline: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.25) as the only focus state
Code Bad: :focus { outline: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.25); }

Guideline: Keep non-text UI visible in both themes
Description: Borders, icons and control boundaries that carry information need contrast against their own background in every palette
Do: Check border, icon and focus-ring tokens against the surface they sit on, not just the text pair
Don't: Reuse one border token for the light and dark palette without re-checking contrast
Code Bad: :root { --border: #e3e6ea; }  # the same light border on a dark surface

Guideline: Hold pointer targets at 24 by 24 CSS pixels
Description: Small hit areas - an icon-only clear button, a table-row delete link - fail the minimum target size unless spacing is used
Do: Give compact controls a 24 by 24 hit area through padding or min-inline-size tokens
Don't: Ship an icon-only button whose glyph size is the hit area
Code Bad: .icon-button { padding: 0; font-size: 12px; }

Guideline: Hold body text at 4.5 to 1
Description: Body text and its background must clear the contrast minimum in every palette the app ships, including swapped fragments
Do: Pair each text token with the surface it renders on and check the pair, not the hex
Don't: Judge contrast on the light palette alone and let the dark block drift
Code Bad: #8a919c body copy on #f4f5f7, a 2.91:1 pairing

Guideline: Keep focus order sensible after a swap
Description: Focus must still move in a meaningful order when htmx replaces a region, or the keyboard lands somewhere unexpected
Do: Swap the smallest region that changed and leave the focused control in place
Don't: Re-render the entire page body on every interaction and drop focus to the document root
Code Bad: Div(hx_get=quotes_page.to(page=2), hx_target="body", hx_swap="innerHTML")

Guideline: Check which htmx build the app loads
Description: The default head injects a pinned htmx 2.0.7 script and htmx4=True swaps in the 4.x build, so attribute semantics and generated classes depend on which one shipped
Do: Read the injected script src, or the fast_app flag, before applying an attribute recipe from a versioned htmx reference
Don't: Assume the pinned build tracks whichever htmx docs page you last read
Code Bad: app, rt = fast_app()  # written against the htmx 4 reference, shipped on the default 2.0.7 build

Guideline: Only fast_app injects the base stylesheet
Description: The base stylesheet is added by the fast_app helper, so an app built from FastHTML() directly and served with serve() gets no base CSS at all
Do: Build the app with fast_app when you want the default base layer, or add the stylesheet link yourself
Don't: Compare an app that uses FastHTML() with one that uses fast_app() and conclude the styles are unreliable
Code Good: app, rt = fast_app(pico=False, hdrs=(css,))  # without fast_app: FastHTML(hdrs=(Link(rel="stylesheet", href="/css/pico.min.css"), css))
Code Bad: app = FastHTML(); serve(app=app)  # no base stylesheet, so every unstyled default shows
